solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Beg audibly for quarry

indicators.note: audibly says we want a word that sounds like the one the clue gives, not its spelling

parts.note: to beg is to pray, plead

explanation.surface: Someone pleading loudly to be given their quarry.
explanation.definitionFit: A hunter's quarry is the animal pursued, its prey.

clue.text: Top nun's urge to tour Brazilian port

indicators.note: to tour a place is to go round it, so these letters surround the port

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian port, is Rio for short

explanation.surface: A senior nun longs to visit Rio.
explanation.definitionFit: A prioress is the head of a priory of nuns, ranking just below an abbess.

clue.text: Racecourse some keep so meticulously

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people look after a racecourse with great care.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom Downs in Surrey is the English racecourse that hosts the Derby.

clue.text: Little girl keeping a sort of porcelain bird

indicators.note: keeping means holding the other letters inside it

parts.note: Flo is a short form of the girl's name Florence
Ming is fine Chinese porcelain of the Ming dynasty

explanation.surface: A young girl hangs on to a piece of porcelain shaped like a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The flamingo is a tall pink wading bird.

clue.text: Up-to-date info from US city trial

explanation.surface: News coming out of a court case in an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: The latest is the most recent news, as in 'have you heard the latest?'

clue.text: Successfully learn short musical work, an outstanding creation

parts.note: to master a skill is to learn it fully
a piece is a short musical composition

explanation.surface: A pianist mastering a brief composition that is a great work.
explanation.definitionFit: A masterpiece is a work of exceptional skill, an artist's finest achievement.

clue.text: Strange thing that is worn in retirement?

definitions.note: a noun is meant: something worn when one retires to bed

indicators.note: strange suggests the letters of the next word are put into an odd new order

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: An odd garment that older people put on once they stop working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retirement' suggests leaving work, but here it is going to bed for the night.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightie is a nightdress, a garment slept in after retiring for the night.

clue.text: Female, heading off for Arabian sultanate

indicators.note: with its head taken off, the word loses its first letter

explanation.surface: A woman sets off for a Gulf country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading off' looks like setting out on a journey, but it means removing the front letter of WOMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Oman is a sultanate on the south-east coast of the Arabian peninsula.

clue.text: Visible perspicacity

definitions.meaning: first meaning: read as two words, ..., able to be seen
second meaning: keen understanding, read as one word

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense only works when the answer is split into two words; the second takes it whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Insight is clear understanding, the sharp perception that perspicacity names, while 'in sight' means able to be seen.

clue.text: Sandy needs money to make flavoured cake

explanation.surface: A baker called Sandy needs cash to make a cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sandy' reads as a person's name, but it describes reddish hair colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Gingerbread is a cake or biscuit spiced with ginger.

clue.text: Greek character American soldiers backed

indicators.note: backed means turned back to front, read from the end

explanation.surface: A Greek figure whom US troops supported.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backed' looks like supported, but it reverses AMGIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sigma is the eighteenth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Bringing back memories about slight smell?

explanation.surface: A faint odour that stirs nostalgia.
explanation.definitionFit: Something reminiscent of the past evokes recollections, calling earlier days to mind.

clue.text: Part of book removed from a theatregoer, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a section of extra material at the end of a book
second meaning: the organ cut out of a patient in an operating theatre

explanation.walkthrough: A theatregoer sounds like someone at a play; here it is a patient taken into an operating theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both supplementary matter after a book's text and the small organ surgeons take out.

clue.text: Sailors observed going about in the morning

indicators.note: going about means wrapping round the other letters

explanation.surface: Sailors spotted wandering around at dawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Seamen are mariners, men who work at sea.

clue.text: A married woman's vast place across the pond

parts.note: Erica is a woman's name; the 's reads as 'is'

explanation.surface: A wife's huge home over the Atlantic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Across the pond' is a British phrase for over the Atlantic Ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Seen from Britain, America is the huge country on the far side of the Atlantic.

clue.text: Fortified building with increased running costs

parts.note: a keep is the strong central tower of a castle

explanation.surface: A castle whose running costs have gone up.
explanation.definitionFit: Upkeep is the cost of maintaining something in working order.

clue.text: Fabric produced by girl briefly engaged by company

indicators.note: engaged by means held inside the other word
briefly means cut short, losing the last letter

explanation.surface: Cloth made by a young woman who has been hired by a firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engaged' suggests hired or betrothed, but here it means held inside the company abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Calico is a plain cotton cloth.

clue.text: Reformed rabble came east, suitable for hugging

indicators.note: reformed means formed again, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A mob that has mended its ways arrives from the east, now cuddly.
explanation.definitionFit: Embraceable means fit to be held close in the arms.

clue.text: Cry out, securing end of major punch-up

indicators.note: securing means holding the other letter fast inside

parts.note: to bawl is to cry out loudly

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Someone shouts as a major fight starts.
explanation.definitionFit: A brawl is a noisy fight, a punch-up.

clue.text: Cotton on small shoot

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to realise or understand, a verb
second meaning: a slender branch of a plant

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cotton' tempts a plant reading alongside the shoot, but 'cotton on' is an idiom for understanding.
explanation.definitionFit: To twig is informal for grasping something, and a twig is also a small woody stem.

clue.text: Grumble when husband gets in hock, perhaps

indicators.note: gets in means the letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: hock is a German white wine, so an example of wine

explanation.surface: A wife complains when her man pawns things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In hock' suggests pawned or in debt; hock is a white wine from the Rhine.
explanation.definitionFit: To whine is to complain in a peevish way.

clue.text: N Atlantic island, one originally colonised by large antelope

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of the next word

parts.note: the eland is a large African antelope

explanation.surface: An island first settled by a big antelope.
explanation.definitionFit: Iceland is an island nation in the North Atlantic, just south of the Arctic Circle.

clue.text: £1,000 initially spent on young relative

parts.note: a grand is slang for a thousand pounds

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A thousand pounds lavished on a youngster in the family.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandson is the son of one's child, a younger family member.

clue.text: Fine loose fibre

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine loose' reads as describing the fibre, but each word gives letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Flax is the plant fibre spun into linen.
